title: ci: only the nightly runs everything. Per-push and PR CI (ci.yml) keep the fast jobs, while a new nightly workflow (schedule plus workflow_dispatch, on the consolidation branch and main) runs the full suites: the bash, Windows PowerShell and PowerShell 7 wrapper postflights and the other long steps
description:
Filed by the governor (governor-e6142a94) on 2026-11-04 from two human rulings: "gates should be 20min tops" (18:07Z) and "only nightly should run all" (18:10Z). The matching global rail is proposal prop-bb985ab8.

WHY
- ci.yml runs everything on every push to PR #230 (moe/work-2026-10-24 into main). The concurrency group replaces only the queued run, so a run completes only every ~4 h. Hardly any landing gets its own CI result.
- The long poles are the three wrapper postflight steps of build-all-platforms. Measured on real runners on 11-04:
  - "Test Bash wrapper postflight and parity" on ubuntu: 44:48-45:50.
  - "Test Windows PowerShell wrapper postflight": hit the 60-min cap at lastScenario P, about 3350 of postflight.ps1's 6165 lines. After d36d5bb7 it has a 180-min cap, an estimated 85-100 min.
  - "Test PowerShell 7 wrapper postflight and parity": an estimated 90-108 min.
- Everything else is minutes: builds, lint, daemon/proxy/claude-plugin tests with coverage, the launcher node tests, the landing guards, VS Code startup and package, the JetBrains build, fresh-linux-install.

CHANGE
1. ci.yml (pull_request and push to main): keep every job and step EXCEPT the long ones. Drop at least the three wrapper postflight steps. Time each remaining step from the last completed runs (gh.exe run view <id> --json jobs, e.g. 41848822541 and 41862780104) and move any other step over about 10 min.
   - Target: every PR job finishes in at most about 20 minutes.
   - Keep the concurrency group.
2. A new .github/workflows/nightly.yml:
   - triggers: `schedule` (one nightly cron, chosen and documented) plus `workflow_dispatch` with a `ref` input;
   - runs everything: today's full ci.yml jobs, including the three wrapper postflights on their OSes and engines;
   - default ref: the consolidation branch, read from a repository variable (for example vars.NIGHTLY_REFS, default 'main'), so main and moe/work-2026-10-24 can both be tested.
   - Note in the file: GitHub fires `schedule` only from the default branch's copy, so the nightly starts firing once PR #230 has merged. workflow_dispatch can be used before that.
   - Share the step definitions instead of copying ~300 lines, for example a reusable workflow (`workflow_call`) that ci.yml and nightly.yml both call with a `full: true|false` input. Your choice; justify it in the plan.
3. Tests that read ci.yml must keep passing and must not lose their meaning. A test asserting "CI runs this suite" must accept nightly.yml where the suite moved. These files read .github/workflows or ci.yml:
   - scripts/tests/daemon-json-cap.test.mjs, seat-registration.test.mjs, runtime-requirements.test.mjs, usage-receipt.test.mjs;
   - local-runner-agents, -bundle, -check, -pinned-client, -seat-capacity, -seat and -snapshot .test.mjs.
4. Docs: the CI paragraph in CLAUDE.md, plus docs/DEVELOPMENT.md and docs/RELEASING.md wherever they describe what CI runs. Generated init files are only touched if a role doc changes, and none should.

OUT OF SCOPE
- release.yml, docker.yml and pages.yml are unchanged. release.yml still builds everything on v* tags.
- Make no GitHub API settings changes, such as required checks or rulesets. Name any the human should make in the summary.

GATE. This row follows the same 20-min rule: actionlint, if installed, or a YAML parse of every workflow; the ci-reading node tests above; and npm run lint. The real proof is the next PR #230 CI run, which the governor watches.
definitionOfDone: ci.yml (pull_request and push to main) no longer runs the three wrapper postflight steps or any other step over about 10 min. Using step timings from real runs, the plan shows every remaining PR job at about 20 min or less.

nightly.yml runs on schedule and on workflow_dispatch (with a ref input) and executes the full set, including the bash, WinPS and PS7 wrapper postflights. Its header documents the default-branch rule for schedule. Shared steps are not copy-pasted, or the plan justifies the duplication.

Every scripts/tests file that reads the workflows passes and still asserts something real: a suite moved to the nightly is asserted there. CLAUDE.md, DEVELOPMENT.md and RELEASING.md describe the PR-versus-nightly split. The gate finishes in 20 min or less.

implementationPlan.description:
ci.yml becomes the one definition of every job, callable with full: true; pull_request and push runs skip only the long suites. All edits are in .github/workflows/ci.yml. A dry-run diff at edc3e937 is /mnt/d/moe-scratch/plan-669e/ci.yml.diff, and the full file is /mnt/d/moe-scratch/plan-669e/ci.yml (sha256 94273943...). Write with your editing tool, never cp: a shell copy leaves no TOOL witness.

(a) Header and triggers. Add a 5-line comment above `on:`: pull requests and pushes to main run the fast set, every step except those guarded by `inputs.full`. nightly.yml calls this file with full: true, which adds the bash, Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7 wrapper postflights (about 45, 85-100 and 90-110 min on hosted runners, too long for a per-push run). Keep `push`/`pull_request` `branches: [main]` byte-for-byte, then add:
```
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      full:
        description: Also run the long suites (the three wrapper postflights).
        type: boolean
        default: false
      ref:
        description: The branch, tag or SHA to check out; empty checks out the triggering event's ref.
        type: string
        default: ''
      artifact-suffix:
        description: Appended to every artifact name, so a run that calls this file more than once keeps the names unique.
        type: string
        default: ''
  # A full run of a branch's own definitions, before nightly.yml is on main:
  #   gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <branch> -f full=true
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      full:
        description: Also run the long suites (the three wrapper postflights).
        type: boolean
        default: true
```

(b) Concurrency. Keep the comment and add the line "A nightly call appends the ref it tests, so its refs never queue behind each other." Set the group to `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}-${{ inputs.ref }}`. On pull_request and push, inputs.ref is '', so a PR still has one group. Do not add cancel-in-progress.

(c) All 5 `- uses: actions/checkout@v7` steps get `with:` / `ref: ${{ inputs.ref }}`: fresh-linux-install, build-typescript, test-typescript, build-plugin and build-all-platforms. An empty ref means the event's ref, so PR checkouts do not change.

(d) The 5 upload-artifact names get `${{ inputs.artifact-suffix }}`: daemon-dist, proxy-dist, daemon-coverage, proxy-coverage and jetbrains-plugin. upload-artifact v4+ refuses a duplicate name within one run, and the nightly calls this file once per ref inside one run. Nothing downloads these artifacts by name: only ci.yml names them.

(e) Replace the three wrapper postflight steps (ci.yml:310-331) with these six, in this order:
```
      - name: Test Bash worktree landing and parity
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          bash scripts/tests/worktree-landing.sh
          bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh

      - name: Test Bash wrapper postflight (nightly)
        # About 45 min on ubuntu-latest: only the nightly runs it.
        if: inputs.full && runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs bash

      - name: Test Windows PowerShell worktree landing
        # About 4 min. PowerShell 7's run of the same file is nightly-only, to keep this job near 20 min.
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        run: powershell -NoProfile -File scripts/tests/worktree-landing.ps1

      - name: Test Windows PowerShell wrapper postflight (nightly)
        # 85-100 min on windows-latest: only the nightly runs it.
        if: inputs.full && runner.os == 'Windows'
        run: node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs powershell

      - name: Test PowerShell 7 parity
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        run: pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts/tests/parity-check.ps1

      - name: Test PowerShell 7 worktree landing and wrapper postflight (nightly)
        # 90-110 min on windows-latest: only the nightly runs it.
        if: inputs.full && runner.os == 'Windows'
        run: |
          pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts/tests/worktree-landing.ps1
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }
          node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs pwsh
```
Error handling:
- A single-command step's exit code is the step's result on both default shells: bash -e on Linux, and on Windows the runner's pwsh wrapper exits with $LASTEXITCODE.
- The two-command pwsh step keeps the explicit LASTEXITCODE stop, so a worktree-landing failure never reaches the postflight.
- On pull_request and push the inputs context is empty, so inputs.full is null and the nightly-only steps show as skipped.

(f) In build-typescript, directly after its Setup Node.js step, add:
```
      - name: Test the PR and nightly workflow split
        run: node --test scripts/tests/ci-workflows.test.mjs
```

Everything else stays byte-for-byte: every other step, `if:`, run line, `node-version: '24'` and the step order. Existing tests depend on it:
- daemon-json-cap and seat-registration require their step in build-all-platforms with `if: runner.os != 'macOS'`.
- Five local-runner tests match the 'Test local runner prerequisite bundles' run line with a regex.
- local-runner-check TC1 requires every node-version to be '24'.

PR job times after this change, from real step timings (runs 41848822541, 41862780104 and 41746515589):
- fresh-linux-install 1.0 min, build-typescript 0.4, test-typescript 3.5, build-plugin 2.8.
- Build (ubuntu): 48.4 - 43.5 (the Bash postflight step) + 1.5 (worktree-landing.sh) = about 6.4.
- Build (windows): 10.9 (steps 1-20) + 3.9 (5.1 worktree-landing.ps1, 15:14:00-15:17:53 in 41848822541) + under 0.1 (parity-check.ps1, 1 s locally) + 0.8 (VS Code startup) = about 16.
- Build (macos): 5.2, unchanged.

The longest remaining PR step is 3.9 min. Keeping pwsh 7's worktree-landing.ps1 in PR would put Windows at about 20 min with no margin, so that run moves to the nightly; the 5.1 run stays.

implementationPlan.description:
New .github/workflows/nightly.yml. It is a caller only and copies no steps, so ci.yml stays the one definition. Write exactly this, with your editing tool (dry-run copy: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/plan-669e/nightly.yml):
```
name: Nightly

# The full CI set once a night: everything ci.yml runs on a pull request, plus the
# long suites it skips there (the bash, Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7
# wrapper postflights). It calls ci.yml with full: true instead of copying its
# steps, so ci.yml stays the one definition of every job.
#
# Default-branch rule: GitHub fires `schedule` only from the default branch's
# (main's) copy of this file, and the Actions tab offers "Run workflow" only for a
# file on main too. So the nightly starts once this file reaches main (PR #230).
# Until then, run a branch's own full set with:
#   gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <branch> -f full=true
# The step definitions come from the commit that started the run (main's for the
# schedule, the chosen branch's for a dispatch), never from the ref under test:
# a step added on another branch joins the nightly once it reaches main.
#
# Refs: the schedule tests each ref in the repository variable NIGHTLY_REFS, a
# JSON array such as ["main","moe/work-2026-10-24"] (unset: ["main"]). A value
# that is not a JSON array fails the run when the matrix is expanded. A dispatch
# with a ref tests only that ref:
#   gh workflow run nightly.yml -f ref=moe/work-2026-10-24
on:
  schedule:
    # 03:17 UTC daily, off the top of the hour, when GitHub delays scheduled runs most.
    - cron: '17 3 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      ref:
        description: The branch, tag or SHA to test; empty tests each ref in vars.NIGHTLY_REFS (default main).
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  full:
    name: Full CI (${{ matrix.ref }})
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        ref: ${{ fromJSON(inputs.ref && format('["{0}"]', inputs.ref) || vars.NIGHTLY_REFS || '["main"]') }}
    uses: ./.github/workflows/ci.yml
    with:
      full: true
      ref: ${{ matrix.ref }}
      # Artifact names must be unique within a run, and each ref's call uploads the same set.
      artifact-suffix: -${{ strategy.job-index }}
```
Why each piece:
- matrix.ref, not a hard-coded branch: the consolidation branch changes over time. The human sets NIGHTLY_REFS; this task changes no settings.
- strategy.job-index for the suffix: refs contain '/', which artifact names refuse.
- No concurrency here: a caller group equal to the called group deadlocks, and ci.yml's group already carries inputs.ref, so two refs never queue behind each other.
- permissions contents: read: a scheduled run that checks out any ref gets a read-only token. Nothing in ci.yml writes with GITHUB_TOKEN; artifacts and caches use the runner token.
- No `if:` for forks: GitHub disables schedules in forks.

Error handling, all loud on the run page:
- A malformed NIGHTLY_REFS fails the expression at matrix expansion.
- A ref that does not exist fails at checkout.
- A dispatch ref containing a double quote breaks fromJSON and fails the run. It never tests something else.

The full Windows job is about 11 + 4 + 84-100 + 4 + 90-108 + 1 = 195-230 min, under GitHub's 360-min job limit.
implementationPlan.note: New nightly.yml written with Write: schedule cron '17 3 * * *' + workflow_dispatch(ref), permissions contents: read, one job `full` (fail-fast false, matrix.ref from inputs.ref / vars.NIGHTLY_REFS / ["main"]) calling ./.github/workflows/ci.yml with full: true, ref: matrix.ref, artifact-suffix: -strategy.job-index. Header documents the default-branch rule for schedule. Byte-identical to the planned draft; PyYAML parses it.

New scripts/tests/ci-workflows.test.mjs = the planned draft (logic unchanged) with R1:-R6: row labels added to the six test names (repo row-id convention, e.g. usage-receipt's 'G1:'), so the contract's 'R2 proves it' / 'R5 proves it' are traceable. implementationPlan.description:
Verification: run checkRefs[0] once, fresh, from the task worktree root, and submit its result as complete_task evidence. It takes about 5 s. Expected output, in order:
- `YAML OK 5`: PyYAML 6.0.1 is installed on this host, and the parse covers ci, docker, nightly, pages and release.
- ℹ pass 38, fail 0: ci-workflows 6, runtime-requirements 9 and local-runner-snapshot 23.
- ℹ pass 17, fail 0: usage-receipt without G1.
- the line `9`: the nine named CI-reading rows passed. These are daemon-json-cap and seat-registration 'CI runs this suite on Linux and Windows', plus local-runner SH4, E8, TC1, MX0, SC0, AS0 and the bundle row.
- PASS parity-check.sh, and npm run lint exit 0.

Error handling. Every piece is chained with && under pipefail, so the first failure stops the gate:
- a YAML error names the file and the line;
- a failing node row names itself;
- any count other than 9 means a CI-reading row failed or vanished. Rerun that node command without the grep to see which. Node counts a file with no matching row as one passing test, so the gate counts the named rows, not '# pass'.

Why those rows and not the whole files: in an unbuilt checkout such as the task worktree, whole daemon-json-cap, local-runner-agents and usage-receipt fail for reasons unrelated to this change, as measured at edc3e937 in an unbuilt clone. The causes are 'build the daemon first' (TY1), onboarding (G1), and the path-contract and named-host identity rows. Their CI-reading rows are what this change can break.

Also check `git diff --stat` against the task branch base: only the 7 paths of this plan. Do not run gh workflow run, set repository variables or change rulesets. Name those in the completion summary as the human's follow-ups: set NIGHTLY_REFS to ["main","moe/work-2026-10-24"]. The PR job names are unchanged, so no required-check edit is needed. A pre-merge full run is `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref moe/work-2026-10-24 -f full=true`. The real proof is the next PR #230 run, every job about 20 min or less with the (nightly) steps skipped, which the governor watches.

implementationPlan.description:
Adversarial self-review of this task's diff, once, at the end. Check each item:
(1) A pull_request or push run executes the same commands as before, minus exactly the four LONG ones. Diff the step list against edc3e937: no other `if:`, run line, node-version or order may change.
(2) inputs.full on events without inputs: the inputs context is empty, `inputs.full` is null and the `&&` is false, so a nightly step is skipped, never failed.
(3) Expression contexts that GitHub checks only at run start:
- `inputs` is allowed in workflow-level concurrency (github, inputs, vars);
- `strategy` and `matrix` are allowed in a reusable-call job's `with:`;
- `inputs` and `vars` are allowed in that job's strategy;
- `strategy` is a supported keyword on a job that calls a reusable workflow;
- hyphenated names (inputs.artifact-suffix, strategy.job-index) are valid dereferences.
A mistake here shows as 'Invalid workflow file' on the next PR #230 push, so re-read every `${{ }}` against those rules.
(4) Collisions when the nightly calls ci.yml twice in one run: artifact names (suffix), the concurrency group (ref suffix), and deadlock (no group in the caller).
(5) Refs: '/' inside branch names works for checkout and for the group string; a malformed NIGHTLY_REFS fails loudly.
(6) The default-branch rule is stated in the header and in DEVELOPMENT.md. Definitions come from the caller commit.
(7) Windows: both new single-command steps exit with the inner process's code, and the pwsh nightly step stops after a failed worktree-landing.ps1.
(8) Does the new test pass when the code does nothing? Re-run at least three of the planned mutations against a scratch copy outside the worktree, never in W: postflight unguarded, full: false, a checkout without ref. Each must fail.
(9) Docs: every number matches step 1's timing table, and no doc says the PR runs a postflight.
(10) Would I be embarrassed if the next PR run failed to start? If any item is doubtful, fix it before complete_task.
implementationPlan.note:
Adversarial self-review, all 10 items:
(1) PyYAML-driven compare vs edc3e937: a PR run's build-all-platforms command sequence (79 commands, with each command's if: guard) equals the old one minus exactly the 4 LONG commands. The other 4 jobs are unchanged except build-typescript's new split-test step. shell/working-directory keys, node-version and job names are unchanged.
(2) A guard without a status function keeps the implicit success(). On PR/push, inputs.full is null, so the nightly steps are skipped, not failed.
(3) Every ${{ }} re-read against GitHub's context table: concurrency (github/inputs/vars), the reusable-call job's strategy (inputs/vars) and with (matrix/strategy), and name (matrix). strategy is supported on a uses: job. Hyphenated dereferences (inputs.artifact-suffix, strategy.job-index) are legal.
(4) Artifacts get -<job-index>, groups get -<ref>, and the caller has no group, so nothing deadlocks.
(5) '/' in refs is fine. A malformed, non-array or empty NIGHTLY_REFS fails at matrix expansion.
(6) The default-branch rule is in the nightly.yml header and in DEVELOPMENT.md.
(7) The Windows single-command steps exit with the inner code through the runner's pwsh LASTEXITCODE epilogue, and the pwsh nightly step has an explicit stop.
(8) Mutations run on /tmp scratch copies, all KILLED: bash postflight unguarded (R2), nightly full:false (R5), a checkout without ref (R4), postflight-safe back in the PR step (R2), a constant suffix (R5), the pull_request trigger dropped (R1), concurrency without the ref (R1), the matrix ignoring NIGHTLY_REFS (R5).
(9) Doc numbers match the timing table. No in-scope doc says PR CI runs a postflight.
Theoretical risks, not fixed (outside the plan):
- The full Windows nightly job is an estimated 195-230 min, but two 180-min postflight-safe caps plus about 15 min could pass GitHub's 360-min job limit in the worst case.
- GitHub probably refuses `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <branch>` until main's ci.yml has workflow_dispatch, so the first full run may be the nightly after PR #230 merges.
The governor's "tests run nowhere" request is already its own row, task-5f5c8999, which depends on this task.

comments.content: Governor, 19:03Z, for the worker and QA on this row. My 18:46Z planning input (comment-b433a3ae) asked this plan to wire the 7 scripts/tests suites that run in no workflow. It came in after revision 1 was planned, and that work is now split into its own row, task-5f5c8999. That row depends on this one and extends ci-workflows.test.mjs once it lands. This row's scope stays exactly revision 1. Don't add the wiring here, and QA should not reject this row for leaving it out.

planSizeWarnings: Plan touches 7 distinct files (target <=5); plans over 10 are rejected. Small file-disjoint tasks review better and parallelize.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: Pull-request and push-to-main CI (ci.yml) runs every job and step it ran before except the long suites. Those are postflight-safe.mjs bash/powershell/pwsh and PowerShell 7's worktree-landing.ps1, and they run only when a caller passes full: true. The fast legs of the three old postflight steps stay in PR CI as their own steps: worktree-landing.sh, parity-check.sh, worktree-landing.ps1 under 5.1 and parity-check.ps1 under 7. A new nightly.yml runs on a daily cron and on workflow_dispatch with a ref input. It calls ci.yml with full: true once per ref in one run, for each ref in vars.NIGHTLY_REFS (default ["main"]); a dispatch ref tests only that ref. Artifact names stay unique per call, and no step is copied. ci.yml also accepts workflow_dispatch (full, default true), so a branch can get its own full run before nightly.yml reaches main. A node test pins the split, and CLAUDE.md, DEVELOPMENT.md and RELEASING.md describe it.
acceptanceCriteria: In ci.yml, the only steps guarded by inputs.full are three nightly-only steps. They hold exactly: postflight-safe.mjs bash (Linux); postflight-safe.mjs powershell (Windows); and pwsh worktree-landing.ps1 followed by postflight-safe.mjs pwsh (Windows). scripts/tests/ci-workflows.test.mjs R2 proves it.

By measured step timings, every PR job takes about 20 min or less: Build (windows) about 16, Build (ubuntu) about 6.4, Build (macos) 5.2, and the others under 4. The longest remaining PR step takes 3.9 min.

nightly.yml has a schedule cron and workflow_dispatch(ref), and one job that calls ./.github/workflows/ci.yml with full: true, ref: matrix.ref and artifact-suffix: -strategy.job-index, with fail-fast false. Its header documents the default-branch rule for schedule. ci-workflows.test.mjs R5 proves it.

The nine CI-reading rows pass unchanged: daemon-json-cap and seat-registration 'CI runs this suite on Linux and Windows', plus local-runner SH4, E8, TC1, MX0, SC0, AS0 and the bundle row. runtime-requirements, local-runner-snapshot and usage-receipt (without the build-dependent G1) also pass.
CLAUDE.md, docs/DEVELOPMENT.md (the smoke-test paragraph and the Windows engines row) and docs/RELEASING.md section 2 describe the PR-versus-nightly split. checkRefs[0] passes in about 5 s.
invariants: A pull_request or push run executes the same commands as before except the four nightly-only ones. No other step's if: guard, run line, node-version or order changes.

PR job names are unchanged (Build (ubuntu-latest), Build (windows-latest), Build (macos-latest), Build TypeScript, Test TypeScript, Build JetBrains Plugin, Fresh Linux installation), so required status checks keep matching.
On a PR run the artifact names are unchanged, because the suffix is empty.
release.yml, docker.yml and pages.yml are untouched, and no GitHub setting, variable or ruleset changes. No role doc or skill changes, so no generated init file changes.
compatibility: PR and push checkouts pass ref '', which is actions/checkout's default (the event's ref), as before.
The concurrency group string changes once, from CI-<pr> to CI-<pr>-; grouping stays per PR and in-progress runs still finish.
approvedScope: nightly.yml (new): the schedule, workflow_dispatch.inputs.ref, permissions contents: read, and the single job `full` (matrix ref, uses ci.yml).
scripts/tests/ci-workflows.test.mjs (new): rows R1-R6. usage-receipt.test.mjs: the G1 comment only.
Docs: the CI sentence in CLAUDE.md, DEVELOPMENT.md's smoke-test paragraph and Windows engines row, and RELEASING.md section 2.
reuse: nightly.yml calls ci.yml as a reusable workflow (workflow_call) instead of copying about 330 lines, so the step definitions stay in one file.
The gate reuses the existing CI-reading rows through --test-name-pattern instead of new copies, and checks their count by name.

daemon-json-cap.test.mjs:675 and seat-registration.test.mjs:330 scan back from their run line to `- name:` and to a 2-space job key, and require build-all-platforms with if: runner.os != 'macOS'.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1. Reusable workflow (chosen). ci.yml gains workflow_call inputs (full, ref, artifact-suffix) and nightly.yml is a short caller. There is one definition, and the PR job names are unchanged.
2. Copy ci.yml into nightly.yml. Rejected: about 330 duplicated lines that drift apart, against the DoD.
3. Composite actions per step group. Rejected: more files, and still two job graphs to keep in step.
4. A postflight-only nightly. Rejected: it would not run everything, and it rebuilds on its own.
5. Keep pwsh 7's worktree-landing.ps1 in PR. Rejected: Windows reaches about 20 min with no margin for runner variance, so that run moves to the nightly and the 5.1 run stays.
6. Concurrency in nightly.yml. Rejected: a caller group equal to the called group deadlocks. The called group already carries the ref.
7. actionlint as the gate. It is not installed here, and the planning session was not allowed to download it. The gate is a PyYAML parse plus the structural node test. The real proof is the next PR #230 run, plus a full dispatch.
8. Assert '# pass 9' for the CI rows. Rejected: node reports a file with no matching row as one passing test, which planning measured, so the gate counts the named rows.

planningNotes.risks:
- GitHub validates expression contexts only at run start. A mistake makes the next PR #230 push fail as 'Invalid workflow file', so re-check every ${{ }} (step 6, item 3); the governor watches that run.
- Pre-merge dispatch: `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <branch>` relies on ci.yml already being registered from main. If GitHub refuses it, the first full run is the nightly after #230 merges, so say that in the summary.
- The nightly runs main's step definitions against the ref under test. A step added on the consolidation branch joins the nightly only after it merges; this is documented.
- permissions contents: read. If a called step needs more in the nightly only (not expected; nothing writes with GITHUB_TOKEN), widen it there, never in ci.yml.
- The full Windows job takes about 3.3-3.8 h, under the 6 h job limit. postflight-safe.mjs still bounds each harness itself.
- The PR concurrency group string changes once, which is harmless.
- Never set NIGHTLY_REFS, trigger runs or edit rulesets from the task: those are human follow-ups.

completionSummary:
PR-vs-nightly CI split, per the approved plan, in 7 paths.
- ci.yml is also a reusable workflow: workflow_call inputs full, ref and artifact-suffix, plus workflow_dispatch with full defaulting to true. The concurrency group ends in -${{ inputs.ref }}. All 5 checkouts take inputs.ref and all 5 artifact names take the suffix.
- The 3 wrapper postflight steps became 6. PR CI keeps worktree-landing.sh + parity-check.sh on Linux, worktree-landing.ps1 under 5.1 and parity-check.ps1 under 7. Under inputs.full only: postflight-safe bash, postflight-safe powershell, and pwsh worktree-landing.ps1 + postflight-safe pwsh.
- New nightly.yml: cron '17 3 * * *' + workflow_dispatch(ref), contents: read. One matrix job calls ci.yml with full: true per ref from NIGHTLY_REFS (default ["main"]). The header documents the default-branch rule.
- New scripts/tests/ci-workflows.test.mjs, rows R1-R6, run in build-typescript.
- usage-receipt G1 comment fix; docs in CLAUDE.md, DEVELOPMENT.md and RELEASING.md.

Evidence:
- The gate passes in about 5 s: YAML OK 5; 38/0; 17/0; the 9 named CI-reading rows; parity PASS; lint OK.
- RED: R1, R2, R4 and R6 fail on edc3e937's ci.yml.
- 8 mutations, all killed.
- A PyYAML compare shows a PR run's commands and guards equal edc3e937's minus exactly the 4 long ones. Job names are unchanged.

Human follow-ups:
- Set the repo variable NIGHTLY_REFS to ["main","moe/work-2026-10-24"].
- No required-check or ruleset change is needed.
- `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref moe/work-2026-10-24 -f full=true` may be refused until main's ci.yml has workflow_dispatch. If so, the first full run is the nightly after PR #230 merges.
- The real proof is the next PR #230 run.

Risk: worst case, the Windows nightly job could pass the 360-min job limit (two 180-min postflight-safe caps); the typical estimate is 195-230 min.
